# Vijaya Sutta (Snp 1.11 (PTS Snp 34))

**ID:** Snp 1.11 (PTS Snp 34)  
**Section:** Suttanipāta (snp)  
**Collection:** Sutta  
**Title (Pali):** Vijaya Sutta

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Vijaya Sutta* ("Victory", Sn 1.11, verses 193–206) is the eleventh discourse of the *Uragavagga* in the *Suttanipāta* [Hinüber 1996; Barua 1921]. In Burmese and manuscript traditions it also bears the alternative title *Kāmavicchandanikasutta* (or *Vicchindanikasutta*) [Bendall 1893; Katre 1931]. In the commentary *Paramatthajotikā II*, an unusual double *uppatti* (occasion of delivery) is postulated for this text [Hinüber 1996].

**Sources**

- [Bendall 1893] Cecil Bendall, Catalogue of Sanskrit, Pali, and Prakrit Books in the British Museum (1893) — Attestation of the alternative title Vichchhindanikasutta and Burmese translations.
- [Katre 1931] S. M. Katre, Early Buddhist Ballads and Their Relation to Older Upanishadic Literature (1931) — Alternative title Kāmavicchandanikasutta and thematic focus on the worthlessness of the body.
- [Hinüber 1996] Oskar von Hinüber, A Handbook of Pāli Literature (1996) — Verse numbering (Sn 193–206) and note on the double uppatti in Paramatthajotikā II.
- [Anālayo 2014] Bhikkhu Anālayo, Perspectives on Satipaṭṭhāna (2014) — Details on the nine bodily orifices discharging impurity and comparison with Ekottarika-āgama.
- [Barua 1921] Benimadhab Barua and Sailendranath Mitra, Prakrit Dhammapada (1921) — Textual identification as Snp No. 11, relation to kāyānupassanā/kāyagatāsati, and cemetery vocabulary.
- [Huynh 2011] Trung Huynh, Reappraisal of Kumarajiva’s Role in Medieval Chinese Buddhism (2011) — Investigation of outer anatomical parts, inner organs, and bodily liquids.
